item.title: How new legislation is helping R.I. fight off invasive green crabs
item.description: Green crabs have resided in New England waters for hundreds of years, but a new law - effective at the beginning of this year - is aiming to reduce the presence of the invasive species.The law authorizes the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management to offer $10 commercial licenses to harvest green crabs. item.title: Letter: Response to Dec. 13 mass shooting
item.description: To The Editor:Anyone who has experienced gun violence knows that there is a 'before' and 'after' to the tragedy.Before Dec. 13, you might have been aware of where the doors were in your classrooms, but never thought you'd have to build barricades against them. Before, the library was a place for studying, not for hiding and getting panicked texts from friends and family. Before, campus safety alerts might have been emails you skimmed, not ones you obsessively checked for law enforcement updates.

item.title: Brown Market Shares Program reaches 20 years of feeding the Brown community
item.description: Most days of the week, The Gate, a multipurpose space located on the ground floor of Alumnae Hall, lies nearly empty. But every Thursday, the room is filled with fresh produce from farms across Rhode Island and Massachusetts.For the past 20 years, the Brown Market Shares Program has provided locally sourced food for Brown students, staff and community members.The BMSP is a recognized food hub by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
